source_title: Govt to spend Rs 14cr on surveys to assess impact of guarantee schemes, insists its not an election-drive - The Times of India
source_excerpt: Bengaluru: The govt will conduct an âimpact assessmentâ of all its social security and populist schemes, including its five flagship guarantees.Briefing reporters after a cabinet meeting Thursday, parliamentary affairs minister Krishna Byre Gowda said the cabinet cleared Project K-Monitor, which would cost the exchequer Rs 14 crore. Karnataka Monitoring and Evaluation Authority (KMEA) will be the lead agency, and it may hire third-party survey agencies.âThe evaluation will be conducted in two phases over eight months, with 1 lakh respondents in the first phase and 60,000 in the second,â Byre Gowda said.He said the exercise would capture citizensâ experience, quality of service delivery, inclusion and exclusion issues, complaints and other administrative outcomes through independent and continuous evaluation. âSurveys will be conducted by the Prajaseva department concerned and a report submitted to the govt,â he said.Asked why the govt was launching the exercise less than two years before the assembly elections, Byre Gowda said it was meant to showcase the difference each scheme had made to peopleâs lives and to identify where the govt needs to improve delivery.He dismissed suggestions that the survey was an election-driven attempt to woo beneficiaries, saying the govt already had complete access to datasets of every scheme. âWe only want to understand the impact they have had on peopleâs lives,â he said.Meanwhile, the cabinet deferred a decision on hiking bus fares, posting it for detailed deliberations as concerns mounted over sustainability of road transport corporations.The cabinet also approved detailed project reports for two water reservoirs to be built by Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB) at a total cost of Rs 61.5 crore.
